title: Holidaying
description: Talk and write about holidays, then and now: read a ranking table of summer outings (positions, equal ranks marked with "=", comparing two columns), describe a holiday with the words that judge it (exciting, interesting, boring, enjoyable, monotonous, relaxing, active, lazy, cheap, expensive, plain, original) and sort activities into active and lazy holidays, express habit in the past with "used to" + base form (affirmative, "didn't use to", "Did you use to…?", repeated actions and states that are no longer true) and with "would" + base form for repeated actions only, keep the past simple for a single finished event, put yesterday and today side by side with the contrast linkers whereas, while, but, however, in contrast and unlike, recognise a text type from its format and content (who writes to whom, spoken or written, postcard, letter, notice, leaflet), and keep the same form all the way through a sentence with parallelism
sources: Official programme transcript - content/programmes-officiels/programme/bac-math/anglais.md, Unit 1 UNIT OUTLINE (p. 36) and Unit 1 lesson 1 "Holidaying" (p. 37-40), plus GRAMMAR REFERENCE "USED TO + VERB" (ADD-ONS, p. 263-264)
